Reproducing Li, Namburi, Olson et al. (2022) from dandiset 000689¶

Paper. Li H, Namburi P, Olson JM, et al. (2022). Neurotensin orchestrates valence assignment in the amygdala. Nature 608, 586-592. doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04964-y. The claims file was written from the accepted author manuscript in PubMed Central (PMC9583860): main text, Methods with the per-panel statistics, and the legends of Figures 1 to 5 and Extended Data Figures 1 to 10.

Dandiset. DANDI:000689, version 0.240530.1923. The paper cites no DANDI version (it predates the dandiset, created in October 2023). There are two published versions, 0.240524.2012 and 0.240530.1923; the data check below shows that both list the same 85 assets with the same asset identifiers, so they do not differ in content. The most recent, 0.240530.1923, is pinned, as the protocol asks when the paper cites none.

This notebook tests the electrophysiology, behavior and NT sensor photometry claims that the files can support, and shows why the others are blocked.

What the dandiset holds. 31 sessions of BLA recordings during the three-cue discrimination task (one per mouse, spike times of 1902 units, trial events, DeepLabCut pose in 29 of them), two pose-only files for other sessions of two of those mice, 32 videos, and 20 photometry sessions of the GRAB-NTS1.0 NT sensor in the BLA (5 mice, early and late acquisition of tone-sucrose and tone-airpuff learning). No file says which mice are CRISPR and which are controls, nor which projection (NAc or CeA) was tagged in each mouse, the units are not the paper's sorted single units, and the pose has no timestamps, so its clock is fitted to the trial table (data check).

for e in E:

Checked against the paper. The session description says sucrose, neutral and shock CSs at 2:1:1, and 25 sessions hold 60, 30 and 30 CSs (some with one or two fewer), as the Methods give (120 trials). Six sessions (H09 to H14, recorded on 2019-08-30, "Disc4") hold 75 sucrose and 45 shock CSs and no neutral CS: the description does not fit them. Every file gives the genotype as "Wild type"; none says whether the mouse is in the CRISPR or the control group, nor whether Cav2-Cre was put in the NAc or the CeA, which the group comparisons and the phototagging need. There are 31 mice where the paper reports 30. H28 and H32 also have a pose-only file for a later discrimination day (Disc4, Disc6) than their recording (Disc3, Disc5), so their recorded session may not be the last day, which is the only day the paper analyses. Each session holds about 850 light events (the phototagging sessions); no "fake" session is labelled.

# Are the units sorted single units? Refractory violations and spikes shared between units.
def coinc(a, b, w=1e-4):
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) < 2: return 0.0
    j = np.clip(np.searchsorted(b, a), 1, len(b) - 1)
    return float(np.mean(np.minimum(np.abs(b[j] - a), np.abs(b[j - 1] - a)) < w))
def unit_quality(e):
    sp = e["spikes"]
    isi = [np.mean(np.diff(s) < 0.001) if len(s) > 1 else np.nan for s in sp]
    allsp = np.concatenate(sp)
    shared = 1 - len(np.unique(np.round(allsp * 30000).astype(np.int64))) / len(allsp)
    nn = min(len(sp), 16)
    pair = [coinc(sp[i], sp[j]) for i in range(nn) for j in range(nn) if i != j]
    return {"subject": e["subject"], "units": len(sp), "median_frac_isi_lt_1ms": np.nanmedian(isi),
            "units_with_isi_viol_gt_5pct": int(np.sum(np.array(isi) > 0.05)),
            "frac_spike_samples_shared": shared, "median_pair_coincidence_0.1ms": np.median(pair)}
with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
    q = pd.DataFrame(list(ex.map(unit_quality, E)))
print(q.round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("\nover all units: median fraction of ISIs below 1 ms = %.3f; units with more than 5%% = %d of %d"
      % (q.median_frac_isi_lt_1ms.median(), q.units_with_isi_viol_gt_5pct.sum(), q.units.sum()))
print("units per session: %s" % q.units.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict())

Checked against the paper. The Methods say single units were sorted in Offline Sorter, and the paper analyses 685 neurons from 30 mice (about 23 per mouse). The files hold 1902 units, 64 in 21 of 31 sessions (two per channel of the 32-channel optrode). In 1061 units more than 5% of the inter-spike intervals are below 1 ms (a median of 17 to 35% per session in H01 to H14), which a well-isolated single neuron does not show, and in each session 6 to 65% of spike samples recur in another unit. These are not the paper's sorted single units: they look like unsorted or multi-unit threshold crossings. The claims that use units are tested on them as they are, and this is recorded as a finding.

# Every text field of each recording file, the units and electrodes columns, and the archive's
# per-asset metadata: is there any group (CRISPR, control) or projection (NAc, CeA) label?
# Also every object under acquisition/ and processing/, with its type, and for image containers
# the description and the shape of each image.
import re
def contents(h, path):
    objs, images = [], []
    for top in ("acquisition", "processing"):
        for k in h[top]:
            o = h[top][k]
            nt = nb._s(o.attrs.get("neurodata_type", ""))
            objs.append(f"{top}/{k.split(':')[0]} ({nt})")
            if nt == "ProcessingModule":
                objs += [f"{top}/{k}/{j} ({nb._s(o[j].attrs.get('neurodata_type', ''))})" for j in o]
            if nt == "Images":
                images.append({"subject": path.split("/")[0][4:], "container": k,
                               "description": nb._s(o.attrs.get("description", ""))[:110],
                               "n_images": sum(hasattr(o[j], "shape") for j in o),
                               "first images": "; ".join(f"{j} {tuple(o[j].shape)}" for j in list(o)[:2] if hasattr(o[j], "shape"))})
    return objs, images

def text_fields(path):
    h = nb.open_h5(path)
    out = {}
    def visit(name, obj):
        if isinstance(obj, nb.h5py.Dataset) and obj.dtype.kind in "OSU" and obj.size <= 64 and not name.startswith(("units/", "intervals/", "acquisition/", "processing/")):
            v = obj[()]
            out[name] = " | ".join(str(nb._s(x)) for x in np.atleast_1d(v) if isinstance(nb._s(x), str))
    h["general"].visititems(lambda n, o: visit("general/" + n, o))
    out["session_description"] = nb._s(h["session_description"][()])
    out["units columns"] = ", ".join(sorted(h["units"].keys()))
    out["electrodes columns"] = ", ".join(sorted(h["general/extracellular_ephys/electrodes"].keys()))
    out["electrode locations"] = ", ".join(sorted(set(nb._s(x) for x in h["general/extracellular_ephys/electrodes/location"][:])))
    return out, contents(h, path)
with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
    TF, CT = zip(*ex.map(text_fields, EP))
fields = sorted(set().union(*TF))
for f in fields:
    vals = sorted(set(t.get(f, "(absent)") for t in TF))
    shown = vals if f != "general/experiment_description" else [v[:80] + "..." for v in vals]
    print(f"{f}: {len(vals)} distinct value(s): {shown[:6]}{' ...' if len(vals) > 6 else ''}")
pat = re.compile(r"crispr|control|scrambl|sgrna|guide|nac|accumbens|cea|central amyg|cav2|projection|group", re.I)
hits = sorted({(f, m.group(0)) for t in TF for f, v in t.items() if f != "general/experiment_description" for m in pat.finditer(v)})
print("\nlabel words in the files' fields (experiment_description, the paper's abstract, left out):", hits)
def asset_subject(a):
    r = requests.get(f"{nb.API}/dandisets/{nb.DANDISET}/versions/{nb.VERSION}/assets/{a['asset_id']}/", timeout=60).json()
    return {k: str(v) for k, v in r.get("wasAttributedTo", [{}])[0].items() if k not in ("identifier",)}
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex:
    am = pd.DataFrame(list(ex.map(asset_subject, [a for a in A if a["path"] in EP])))
print("\narchive asset metadata, subject fields:", list(am.columns))
print({c: sorted(am[c].unique().tolist())[:4] for c in am.columns if c not in ("age",)})

counts = pd.Series([x for objs, _ in CT for x in objs]).value_counts()
print("\nobjects under acquisition/ and processing/ (number of the 31 files holding each):")
print(counts.to_string())
imgs = pd.DataFrame([r for _, im in CT for r in im])
print(f"\nimage containers: {len(imgs)} in {imgs.subject.nunique()} files; files without: {[e['subject'] for e, (_, im) in zip(E, CT) if not im]}")
print(imgs.to_string(index=False, max_colwidth=110))
print("image names in all containers:", sorted({re.sub(r"\d+", "#", n.split(" ")[0]) for s in imgs["first images"] for n in s.split("; ")}))

No field of the files, and no subject field of the archive's metadata, names a CRISPR or control group, a guide RNA, or the NAc or CeA (the words found, if any, are listed above with their field). The units table holds only spike times and a unit name; the electrodes table gives no location.

27 of the 31 files (all but H01, H02, H07 and H08) also hold a stack of confocal images (COFAImages, 8 to 42 images each), whose description names an Olympus FLUOVIEW file of the PVT (for example H17PVT_40x.oif). The images are named only by depth (GrayScaleImage1Depth#, and a composite), with no channel, probe or group label.

# Clock check for the spikes and the trial table: CS-evoked change in population rate at the
# true CS onsets against the same onsets shifted 10 s earlier (inside the inter-trial interval).
def pop_resp(e, shift):
    on = np.concatenate([e["trials"][v][0] for v in nb.CS_TYPES.values() if v in e["trials"]]) + shift
    out = []
    for sp in e["spikes"]:
        p = nb.psth(sp, on, 1.0, 1.0, 0.1)
        b = p[:10].mean()
        out.append((p[10:13].mean() - b) / (p[:10].std(ddof=1) + 1e-9))
    return np.median(np.abs(out))
ck = pd.DataFrame([{"subject": e["subject"], "true_onsets": pop_resp(e, 0.0), "shifted_-10s": pop_resp(e, -10.0)} for e in E])
print("median |z| of the 0 to 0.3 s response across units, per session:")
print(ck.round(2).to_string(index=False))
print("sessions where the true onsets give the larger response: %d of %d" % ((ck.true_onsets > ck["shifted_-10s"]).sum(), len(ck)))

The units respond more at the true CS onsets than at onsets shifted into the inter-trial interval in the sessions counted above, which is consistent with the spikes and the trial table sharing a clock (a check that supports, without proving, the alignment). It fails in H17, whose spike times end at 249 s of a 12118 s recording (next cell): its units cannot be aligned with its trials. In H22, H27, H34 and H39 the two values are close, so the alignment is not shown there.

H17's spike times all fall within the first 249 s of a recording of 12118 s, while its trial events cover the whole session: its spike times are not on the trial clock (a file error). Every session holds about 854 light events in two blocks of about 427, which fits the Methods' two light sessions (a "fake" one with the patch cord disconnected, then the real one), but no label says which block is the fake session. In 12 sessions (H31 to H42) one block comes before the task and one after it; the Methods put both after the task.

# Does the pose share the trial clock? The pose series give only a start time (0 s) and a nominal
# 15 frames/s, no timestamps. At each port entry (beam break, trial table) the head should be at the
# port. (1) With the nominal clock, the fixed lag (pose time minus trial time) that minimises the
# median head-to-port distance at port entries, in each third of the session. (2) A linear map,
# pose time = T + offset + factor * (t - T), fitted to all port entries (nb.fit_pose_clock), and
# the best extra lag left in each third under it (0 when the map holds throughout).
def pose_clock(p):
    h = nb.open_h5(p)
    subj = p.split("/")[0][4:]
    if "processing/behavior/PoseEstimation" not in h:
        return subj, None
    pose = nb.load_pose(h); r, t0 = pose["rate"], pose["t0"]
    m = nb.pose_measures(pose)
    dist = m["distance_to_port"]
    tt = h["intervals/trials/trial_type"][:].astype(str); st = h["intervals/trials/start_time"][:]
    pe = np.sort(st[tt == "port_entry"])
    out = {"subject": subj, "pose_s": round(len(dist) / r), "port_entries": len(pe)}
    lags = np.arange(-200, 200.01, 0.2)
    for k, seg in enumerate(np.array_split(pe, 3)):
        med = nb._median_at(dist, r, t0, seg[None, :] + lags[:, None])
        out[f"lag{k + 1}_s"] = round(float(lags[np.nanargmin(med)]), 1)
    c = nb.fit_pose_clock(dist, r, t0, pe)
    out.update({"fit_offset_s": round(c["offset"], 1), "fit_factor": round(c["factor"], 4),
                "resid1_s": c["resid_lag_thirds"][0], "resid2_s": c["resid_lag_thirds"][1], "resid3_s": c["resid_lag_thirds"][2],
                "dist_fit": round(c["med_dist_fit"], 1), "dist_lag0": round(c["med_dist_lag0"], 1), "dist_all_frames": round(c["med_dist_all"], 1)})
    return subj, (out, {"measures": m, "rate": r, "t0": t0, "clock": c})
t = time.time()
with ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
    PC = dict(ex.map(pose_clock, EP))
pl = pd.DataFrame([v[0] for v in PC.values() if v is not None])
print(f"pose read and clocks fitted in {time.time() - t:.0f} s; sessions without pose: {[k for k, v in PC.items() if v is None]}")
print(pl.round(1).assign(fit_factor=pl.fit_factor.round(4)).to_string(index=False))
spread = pl[["lag1_s", "lag2_s", "lag3_s"]].max(axis=1) - pl[["lag1_s", "lag2_s", "lag3_s"]].min(axis=1)
resid = pl[["resid1_s", "resid2_s", "resid3_s"]].abs().max(axis=1)
pl["aligned"] = resid <= 1.0
print("\nnominal clock: median |lag| %.1f s; sessions whose best lag changes by more than 5 s within the session: %d of %d"
      % (np.median(np.abs(pl[["lag1_s", "lag2_s", "lag3_s"]].values)), int((spread > 5).sum()), len(pl)))
print("linear map: sessions with every third within 1 s of the map: %d of %d; not: %s"
      % (pl.aligned.sum(), len(pl), list(pl.subject[~pl.aligned])))
print("fitted factor in the aligned sessions: median %.4f, range %.4f to %.4f; median distance at port entries %.1f px under the map, %.1f px at lag 0, %.1f px over all frames"
      % (pl.fit_factor[pl.aligned].median(), pl.fit_factor[pl.aligned].min(), pl.fit_factor[pl.aligned].max(),
         pl.dist_fit[pl.aligned].median(), pl.dist_lag0[pl.aligned].median(), pl.dist_all_frames[pl.aligned].median()))
print("aligned sessions with a factor between 0.987 and 0.989: %d of %d" % (pl.fit_factor[pl.aligned].between(0.987, 0.989).sum(), pl.aligned.sum()))

import av
def video_info(a):
    out = {"subject": a["path"].split("/")[0][4:], "file": a["path"].split("/")[1][:40], "container": a["path"][-3:]}
    try:
        rf = nb.RangeFile(f"{nb.API}/assets/{a['asset_id']}/download/")
        f = av.open(rf)
        v = f.streams.video[0]
        out.update({"frames": v.frames, "rate": float(v.average_rate), "duration_s": round(f.duration / 1e6, 1) if f.duration else np.nan,
                    "MB_read": round(rf.fetched / 1e6, 1)})
        f.close()
    except Exception as ex:
        out["error"] = str(ex)[:60]
    return out

mkv files report no frame count in their header (0); their rate is the container's nominal one.

With the nominal clock (15 frames per second from 0 s) the head is closest to the port up to 192 s away from the port entries (median 80 s), and the best lag drifts within the session in 28 of 29 sessions (columns lag1 to lag3). A linear map with an offset and a rate factor removes the drift in 21 of the 29 sessions: under it, the best extra lag in each third is within 1 s of zero, 20 of those 21 fitted factors lie between 0.9874 and 0.9885 (H27 is at 1.0000), and the median head-to-port distance at port entries is 38 pixels against 105 over all frames. A common factor of about 0.988 is what a video whose true frame rate is about 1.2% below the nominal 15 per second would give. In H11, H14, H17, H23, H25, H29, H39 and H40 the map leaves a lag of 2.8 to 19.2 s in some third, or the distance stays near that over all frames (H29, H39, H40).

The video headers (next output) give a constant 15 frames per second for the mp4 files and durations within 10 s of the pose series, except H07, H09 and H10, whose videos run 818 to 1528 s longer than their pose, and H11, 426 s longer; the mkv files give no frame count. So the drift is not visible in the files' own metadata; the original videos were .asf files (PoseEstimation original_videos), whose timing is lost. The pose can be put on the trial clock in the 21 aligned sessions, by a map estimated from the data, not given by the files. This is an assumption for the behavior claim, which uses only those sessions. The map is consistent with the data, not shown by them.

Checked against the paper. The files hold the GRAB-NTS1.0 sensor ("neurotensin-fluorescent sensor") in the BLA of five wild-type mice, with 415 and 470 nm excitation, which is the experiment of Figure 3j-l (N = 5; the Methods exclude one of six mice for fiber placement, and the subjects are Mouse1, 2, 4, 5 and 6). Frames come every 16.7 ms (60 Hz), not at the Methods' 40 Hz: one series interleaves three frame types. The LED labels mark every 415 nm frame and every 470 nm frame (a third of the frames each); these sit on a fixed phase of three ("agree" is the fraction of labelled frames on the most common phase). In Mouse6's late sucrose session (M-5) the labels move by one frame after a 2.3 ms frame interval ("labels_moved"), while the data keep their order: the mean of each phase after that interval ("phase_means_after_irregular") is the same as over the session, with the near-constant third frame type still on phase 0. Following the labels there would read that constant frame type as the 470 nm channel, so the channels are taken from the frame order, at the phase the labels give before the first irregular interval. The third frame type is a near-constant value around 0.13 to 0.20 that no metadata describes. Each session holds about 60 cues lasting 1.9 to 2 s, about 30 s apart. The exception is Mouse1's early airpuff session (M-0): it holds 29 cues, and its last three come 4.7 and 7.4 s apart, one of them a 4.7 s bout, which looks like a disrupted end of the session. These cues are among the "all trials" readings; the "first 16 trials" readings do not reach them. The Methods give a 4 s CS with the US 2 s after onset and about half of the CSs unpaired; the files mark one kind of cue, 2 s long, and no US. In sucrose sessions licking rises after the cue ends (frames with a lick 2 to 4 s after onset against the 2 s before), which places the sucrose at the end of the 2 s cue, as the Methods' US time of 2 s gives; no file marks whether a cue was paired or unpaired, nor the airpuff. All cues are therefore analysed as CS-US trials, an assumption recorded with the claims.

In the late sucrose sessions most cues are followed by licking, so the files' cues are mostly, and perhaps all, paired with sucrose; the early sessions, before learning, cannot tell.

Photometry claims (Figure 3j-l)¶

Processing as the claims' criterion gives it (Methods, Fiber photometry, Data analysis): 415 and 470 nm channels median-filtered over 200 ms and averaged into 200 ms (5 Hz) bins from -5 to 10 s around each CS onset; the trial-averaged 470 nm trace regressed on the trial-averaged 415 nm trace over -5 to 0 s (the 415 nm fit subtracted from the 470 nm trace), the residuals z-scored against -5 to 0 s. Windows: CS 0 to 2 s, US 2 to 7 s (Figure 3 legend). Early and late are the files' early and late acquisition sessions. Readings run, as the criterion lists them: (a) first 16 trials or (b) all trials; (i) area under the z-scored curve or (ii) mean z. One more detail the Methods leave open is run both ways: the z-score uses each trial's own baseline ("trial") or the session's pooled baseline ("session"). The regression is fitted on the trial-averaged baseline, as the Methods say; the fitted slope, intercept and correlation of each session are printed, and a fit on the baseline bins of every trial pooled is run as a variant, since the averaged baseline may hold too little variance to fit.

TRIALS, FITS = {}, []
for s in S:
    key = (s["subject"], "sucrose" if "Reward" in s["session_id"] else "airpuff", "early" if "early" in s["session_id"] else "late")
    for zm in ("trial", "session"):
        tb, Z, keep, fit = nb.photometry_trials(s, zmode=zm, return_fit=True)
        TRIALS[key + (zm,)] = (tb, Z)
    tb, Z, keep, fitp = nb.photometry_trials(s, zmode="trial", fit="pooled", return_fit=True)
    TRIALS[key + ("trial, pooled fit",)] = (tb, Z)
    FITS.append({"mouse": key[0], "task": key[1], "phase": key[2], "slope": fit[0], "intercept": fit[1], "r": fit[2],
                 "pooled_slope": fitp[0], "pooled_intercept": fitp[1], "pooled_r": fitp[2]})
print("470 nm on 415 nm regression over -5 to 0 s, per session (trial-averaged fit, and pooled-trials variant):")
print(pd.DataFrame(FITS).round(3).to_string(index=False))
print("trials kept per session (all cues have a full -5 to 10 s window):",
      {f"{k[0]} {k[1]} {k[2]}": v[1].shape[0] for k, v in TRIALS.items() if k[3] == "trial"})
mice = sorted({k[0] for k in TRIALS})

def measure(task, phase, zm, sub, meas, lo, hi):
    out = []
    for m in mice:
        tb, Z = TRIALS[(m, task, phase, zm)]
        Z = Z[:16] if sub == "first16" else Z
        out.append(nb.window_measure(tb, Z, lo, hi, meas).mean())
    return np.array(out)

def compare(task, zmodes=("trial", "session")):
    rows = []
    for zm in zmodes:
        for sub in ("first16", "all"):
            for meas in ("auc", "mean"):
                r = {"zscore": zm, "trials": sub, "measure": meas}
                for win, (lo, hi) in (("US", (2, 7)), ("CS", (0, 2))):
                    e, l = measure(task, "early", zm, sub, meas, lo, hi), measure(task, "late", zm, sub, meas, lo, hi)
                    tt = stats.ttest_rel(l, e)
                    d = l - e
                    ci = stats.t.interval(0.95, len(d) - 1, d.mean(), stats.sem(d))
                    r.update({f"{win}_late-early": d.mean(), f"{win}_ci_low": ci[0], f"{win}_ci_high": ci[1],
                              f"{win}_t": tt.statistic, f"{win}_p": tt.pvalue, f"{win}_mice_in_direction": None})
                    r[f"{win}_mice_up"] = int((d > 0).sum())
                rows.append(r)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).drop(columns=["US_mice_in_direction", "CS_mice_in_direction"])

Result: not reproduced. Under the per-trial z-score the US response to sucrose is larger in the late session under all four readings of the criterion, but p < 0.05 holds only with all trials: AUC +3.53 (95% CI 1.82 to 5.24), t(4) = 5.74, p = 0.0046, 5 of 5 mice higher, inside the paper's CI of 2.744 to 5.538. With the first 16 trials it is AUC +2.94, p = 0.093, 4 of 5 mice higher. AUC and mean give the same t and p, so the two passing readings are one result, and the criterion's "p < 0.05 with late higher under every reading" holds in 2 of its 4 readings: the criterion is not met. The significant result also rests on the regression fitted on the trial-averaged baseline, whose correlation is 0.48 to 0.75 in four sucrose sessions (M-0 early and late, M-1 late, M-3 early); fitted on the pooled baseline bins of every trial (correlation at least 0.938) no reading reaches p < 0.05 (p >= 0.44), and under the session-pooled z-score none does either (p >= 0.16). The CS window does not change under any reading (p >= 0.25), as in the paper. The per-trial z-score is the reading adopted (an assumption: the Methods z-score "using data a baseline window of -5 s to 0 s", most simply read as each trial's own window). The criterion has no partial condition, so with p < 0.05 failing in half its readings, and in every variant of the processing, the claim is not reproduced; only the direction holds throughout.

Result: not reproduced. In the early sessions the mean over mice of the US-window signal is below zero for sucrose under the per-trial z-score (-0.62 with the first 16 trials, -0.40 with all trials) but above zero for airpuff (+0.11 and +0.19; M-4 at +2.15), so the criterion, which needs both below zero, is not met under any per-trial reading. Under the session-pooled z-score the signs change with the trial subset (0 of 8 readings in all). No mean differs from zero (p >= 0.23). Read as a brief dip, the paper's word "transient", the mouse-averaged trace does go below zero within 2 to 7 s for both outcomes under the per-trial z-score (lowest -1.09 for sucrose and -0.63 for airpuff, first 16 trials); whether the criterion's window mean is the right measure for a transient decrease is asked of a reader.

Electrophysiology claims (Figure 4)¶

fig4-recording-count¶

685 BLA neurons were recorded from 30 mice during the three-cue discrimination task. Units from the last discrimination-task session of each mouse, with baseline firing of at least 0.3 Hz (Methods). Whether 685 is counted before or after that exclusion is not said; both counts are shown and either may match (expected 685 +/- 68.5 neurons, 30 +/- 3 mice).

Baseline rate: the mean rate in the 1 s before each CS onset, over all CSs of the session (the PSTH baseline of the Methods); the whole-session rate is shown as a variant.

Result: partially reproduced. The number of mice (31) is within the tolerance of 30. The unit count is not: 1902 units, 1739 with a baseline rate of at least 0.3 Hz (1884 by whole-session rate), against the paper's 685; neither is within 68.5 of 685. The units are not sorted single units (data check), which fits a median of 64 per mouse instead of 23. The 2:1:1 ratio of the statement holds in 25 of 31 sessions; H09 to H14 have no neutral CS.

fig4d-seven-clusters¶

Unsupervised hierarchical clustering of BLA responses to the sucrose, neutral and shock CSs gives seven functional clusters. Per neuron, 20 ms PSTHs from -1 to 1 s around CS onset, z-scored with the 1 s baseline, smoothed with a Gaussian-weighted moving average (smoothing factor 0.85), the three CS traces concatenated; Ward linkage with correlation distance cut at 35% of the maximum linkage distance; readings (a) Ward on the correlation distance matrix, (b) Ward with Euclidean distance on centred, unit-norm rows. Reproduced when one reading gives seven clusters.

Units with a baseline rate below 0.3 Hz are excluded (Methods). The six sessions without neutral CSs cannot give the concatenated trace and are left out; so are units whose baseline SD is zero. The "smoothing factor of 0.85" sets the window through a MATLAB heuristic the paper does not give, so the smoothing window is run over a range (in 20 ms bins, smoothing each CS trace separately).

In [18]:
feats, owner = [], []
dropped = {"low_rate": 0, "no_neutral_session": 0, "zero_sd": 0}
for e in E:
    on = {k: e["trials"][v][0] for k, v in nb.CS_TYPES.items() if v in e["trials"]}
    allon = np.sort(np.concatenate(list(on.values())))
    for u, sp in enumerate(e["spikes"]):
        b = np.mean(np.searchsorted(sp, allon) - np.searchsorted(sp, allon - 1.0))
        if b < 0.3: dropped["low_rate"] += 1; continue
        if "neutral" not in on: dropped["no_neutral_session"] += 1; continue
        z = np.array([nb.zscore_psth(nb.psth(sp, on[k])) for k in ("sucrose", "neutral", "shock")])
        if np.isnan(z).any(): dropped["zero_sd"] += 1; continue
        feats.append(z); owner.append(e["subject"])
F = np.array(feats); owner = np.array(owner)
print("units clustered:", len(F), "from", len(set(owner)), "mice; dropped:", dropped)

def cluster(F, window):
    X = nb.gauss_smooth(F, window).reshape(len(F), -1)
    Za = linkage(pdist(X, "correlation"), "ward")
    ca = fcluster(Za, 0.35 * Za[:, 2].max(), "distance")
    Xc = X - X.mean(1, keepdims=True); Xc /= np.linalg.norm(Xc, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    Zb = linkage(Xc, "ward")
    cb = fcluster(Zb, 0.35 * Zb[:, 2].max(), "distance")
    return ca, cb

rows = []
CL = {}
for w in (1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 15, 21, 31, 41, 51, 75, 101):
    ca, cb = cluster(F, w)
    CL[w] = (ca, cb)
    rows.append({"window_bins": w, "window_ms": w * 20, "clusters_a_corr_ward": ca.max(), "clusters_b_unitnorm_ward": cb.max(),

Result: blocked (methods_underspecified). With the paper's rule (Ward linkage, correlation distance, cut at 35% of the maximum linkage distance) the 1399 units of 24 mice give 8 to 12 clusters under reading (a) and 11 to 14 under reading (b) for smoothing windows of 20 to 420 ms, and 6 to 8 under (a) for windows of 620 ms to 2 s; seven clusters come only under reading (a) with an 820 ms window. The count depends on the smoothing window, which the paper sets by MATLAB's "smoothing factor of 0.85" without the window it produced, so no reading can be preferred; the count also moves with the cut fraction (14 at 25%, 10 at 35%, 7 at 40%, 5 at 50% for a 220 ms window). Without H22, H27, H34 and H39, whose CS alignment is not shown, seven clusters come under (a) at 420 ms and under (b) at 1020 ms and 2 s. Some clusters are single sessions (at 220 ms one cluster is 93% H27), so a count here would not show functional types. The units are not the paper's sorted neurons.

fig4c-photoidentification¶

BLA-NAc and BLA-CeA neurons are identified by short-latency responses to light at the end of each session. The Methods' rule (1 ms PSTH 50 ms around light onset, z-scored against the 50 ms before; excitation above z = 1.98 within 6 ms, none 7 to 50 ms after with a 6 ms moving average, none in the fake session); readings (a) all pulse onsets of the trains and the onset of the long light, (b) the 1 Hz pulses only. Reproduced when the counts are within 10% of 39 BLA-NAc and 32 BLA-CeA neurons under one reading.

No file says which projection (NAc or CeA) carries the Cav2-Cre in each mouse, so the two counts cannot be split. Their sum can still be tested: both counts are within 10% only if the total is within 63.9 to 78.1 (0.9 and 1.1 times 71). The fake-session test needs to know which of the two light blocks is the fake one. The Methods put the fake session first ("a phototagging session was conducted after a 'fake' phototagging session in which the patch cord was disconnected", Methods, In vivo electrophysiology), so block 1 is taken as the fake one; the reverse is run as a reading, and for H31 to H42, where one block comes before the task, either order per session is allowed (the lowest total over those choices is printed). Light events of 5 and 10 ms are the pulses; the files' 100 ms events are the only longer light, and their onsets are added in reading (a).

tag_rows = []
for e in E:
    on, off = e["trials"]["phototagging"]
    dur = off - on
    g = np.argmax(np.diff(on))
    block = [np.arange(len(on)) <= g, np.arange(len(on)) > g]
    def pulses(b, reading):
        p = on[block[b] & (dur <= 0.011)]
        if reading == "a":
            return np.sort(np.r_[p, on[block[b] & (np.abs(dur - 0.1) < 0.01)]])
        return p[(np.r_[np.inf, np.diff(p)] > 0.9) & (np.r_[np.diff(p), np.inf] > 0.9)]
    base = U[U.subject == e["subject"]].baseline_hz.values
    r = {"subject": e["subject"], "units": len(e["spikes"])}
    for rd in ("a", "b"):
        P = [pulses(0, rd), pulses(1, rd)]
        r[f"{rd}_pulses"] = len(P[1])
        # nb.photoresponsive(sp, real, fake) is "responsive to real and not to fake"; computed once per block.
        resp = [np.array([nb.photoresponsive(sp, P[b])[0] for sp in e["spikes"]]) for b in (0, 1)]
        for name, (fk, rl) in {"fake1": (0, 1), "fake2": (1, 0)}.items():
            ok = resp[rl] & ~resp[fk]
            r[f"{rd}_{name}"] = int(ok.sum()); r[f"{rd}_{name}_0.3Hz"] = int((ok & (base >= 0.3)).sum())
        r[f"{rd}_resp_block1"] = int(resp[0].sum()); r[f"{rd}_resp_block2"] = int(resp[1].sum())
    tag_rows.append(r)

Result: blocked, metadata insufficient. With the fake-session test the rule tags 91 to 256 units in total, depending on the reading of the pulses, which block is the fake one, and the 0.3 Hz exclusion: the fewest are 91 (1 Hz pulses, either block order allowed in H31 to H42, baseline at least 0.3 Hz), and with the Methods' order (block 1 fake) 146 and 133 for readings (a) and (b). All are above 78.1. But the test cannot be applied as the Methods mean it. Block 1, taken as the fake session, evokes a short-latency response in 1353 of 1902 units (reading a), and block 2 in 1243; 88% of the units responsive to block 2 also respond to block 1. A session with the patch cord disconnected should evoke no light response, so either neither block is the fake session as the Methods describe it, or the responses are light artefacts on units that are not sorted. The 91 to 256 "tagged" units are then units that cross the threshold in one block and not in the other, and their count does not test the claim. Without labels for the fake and real blocks (and for the projection of each mouse), the claim cannot be tested.

Behavior claim (Figure 5d-h)¶

fig5dh-behavior-clusters¶

Unsupervised trial-by-trial clustering of pose-derived behavior gives seven clusters for sucrose trials and five for shock trials. Eight measures for the 300 frames (20 s) after CS onset; tsfresh features (about 6000); PCA, t-SNE on the top 30 PCs, a kernel density over the t-SNE map (seaborn kdeplot), local maxima as watershed markers; sucrose and shock trials separately. t-SNE perplexity, kernel bandwidth and seed are not given: the defaults are used with several seeds. Reproduced when the default settings give 7 and 5 clusters for most seeds.

The trials come from the sessions where the fitted pose clock holds (data check), with the CS onsets of the trial table mapped onto the pose clock. Choices the paper does not make, each shown: tsfresh 0.16.0 does not install with this Python (3.13), so the current tsfresh with its default, comprehensive feature set is used (6264 features per trial, against the paper's "~6000"); features that are not finite or constant are dropped. Whether the features are scaled before PCA is not said; both are run. The z-scored features are the reading adopted, since on the raw features the PCA sees only the few features with the largest scales and the cluster counts move with changes of 1e-9 in the features (shown below). "The defaults of scikit-learn" are read two ways: the current defaults (PCA initialisation, automatic learning rate), as installed, and those of the scikit-learn releases contemporary with tsfresh 0.16.0 (2020: random initialisation, learning rate 200). The kernel density is seaborn's default (scipy gaussian_kde, Scott's bandwidth, 200 x 200 grid, 3 bandwidths beyond the data), and each local maximum of the grid is one watershed region.

for k, X in BT.items():
    t = time.time()
    df = pd.DataFrame({"id": np.repeat(np.arange(len(X)), X.shape[2]), "time": np.tile(np.arange(X.shape[2]), len(X))})
    for j, m in enumerate(nb.POSE_MEASURES):
        df[m] = X[:, j, :].ravel()
    with warnings.catch_warnings():

        Fk = extract_features(df, column_id="id", column_sort="time", default_fc_parameters=ComprehensiveFCParameters(),
                              n_jobs=4, disable_progressbar=True)
    V = Fk.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    V = V.loc[:, V.notna().all() & (V.std() > 0)]
    FEAT[k] = V
    print(f"{k}: {len(X)} trials, {Fk.shape[1]} features, {V.shape[1]} finite and not constant ({time.time() - t:.0f} s)")

from scipy import ndimage
from threadpoolctl import threadpool_info
def tsne_counts(PCs, seeds=range(5), store=None, **kw):
    """Density peaks of the t-SNE map per seed: all maxima, and maxima above 5% of the highest."""
    counts, counts5 = [], []
    for seed in seeds:
        Y = TSNE(2, random_state=seed, **kw).fit_transform(PCs)
        n, D = nb.density_peaks(Y); counts.append(n)
        counts5.append(int(((D == ndimage.maximum_filter(D, size=3, mode="constant", cval=-np.inf)) & (D > 0.05 * D.max())).sum()))
        if store is not None:
            store[seed] = Y
    return counts, counts5
target = {"sucrose": 7, "shock": 5}
rows = []
EMB = {}
for k, V in FEAT.items():
    for scaling in ("z-scored", "raw"):
        M = ((V - V.mean()) / V.std()).values if scaling == "z-scored" else V.values
        pca = PCA(30, random_state=0).fit(M)
        PCs = pca.transform(M)
        for defaults, kw in (("current", {}), ("2020", {"init": "random", "learning_rate": 200.0})):
            store = {}
            counts, counts5 = tsne_counts(PCs, store=store, **kw)
            EMB.update({(k, scaling, defaults, s): Y for s, Y in store.items()})
            rows.append({"trials": k, "features": scaling, "tsne_defaults": defaults, "pca_solver": pca._fit_svd_solver,
                         "var_30pcs": round(pca.explained_variance_ratio_.sum(), 3), "clusters_by_seed": counts,
                         "clusters_peaks_above_5pct": counts5, "target": target[k], "seeds_at_target": sum(c == target[k] for c in counts)})
bc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(bc.to_string(index=False))
both = {(f, d): (bc[(bc.trials == "sucrose") & (bc.features == f) & (bc.tsne_defaults == d)].seeds_at_target.iloc[0] >= 3,
                 bc[(bc.trials == "shock") & (bc.features == f) & (bc.tsne_defaults == d)].seeds_at_target.iloc[0] >= 3)
        for f in ("z-scored", "raw") for d in ("current", "2020")}
print("\n(sucrose 7 in most seeds, shock 5 in most seeds) per reading:", both)
print("readings with both:", [r for r, v in both.items() if all(v)])
for k in FEAT:
    raw_var = FEAT[k].var().sort_values(ascending=False)
    print(f"{k}, raw features: share of the total variance in the largest 1, 3 and 10 features: "
          f"{raw_var.iloc[0] / raw_var.sum():.4f}, {raw_var.iloc[:3].sum() / raw_var.sum():.4f}, {raw_var.iloc[:10].sum() / raw_var.sum():.4f}; largest: {raw_var.index[0]}")
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 4))
for ax, k in zip(axes, ("sucrose", "shock")):
    Y = EMB[(k, "z-scored", "current", 0)]
    ax.scatter(Y[:, 0], Y[:, 1], s=3, c=pd.factorize(BW[k])[0], cmap="tab20")
    ax.set_title(f"{k} trials, t-SNE (z-scored features, current defaults, seed 0)", fontsize=9); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("colours are mice; all points are plotted")

# Sensitivity to numerical detail that the seeds do not fix, with the current defaults: an exact PCA
# (svd_solver="full") in place of the randomized one PCA(30) chooses here, and each feature
# multiplied by (1 + 1e-9 * standard normal noise) before scaling. Seeds 0 to 2.
print("\nBLAS and OpenMP libraries (the PCA's arithmetic depends on them):",
      [(i.get("internal_api"), i.get("version"), i.get("architecture"), i.get("num_threads")) for i in threadpool_info()])
rng_b = np.random.default_rng(5)
for k, V in FEAT.items():
    noisy = V.values * (1 + 1e-9 * rng_b.standard_normal(V.shape))
    for scaling in ("z-scored", "raw"):
        for name, (Mv, solver) in {"exact PCA": (V.values, "full"), "features x (1 + 1e-9 noise)": (noisy, "auto")}.items():
            Mv = (Mv - Mv.mean(0)) / Mv.std(0, ddof=1) if scaling == "z-scored" else Mv
            counts, _ = tsne_counts(PCA(30, svd_solver=solver, random_state=0).fit_transform(Mv), seeds=range(3))
            print(f"{k}, {scaling} features, {name}: clusters by seed {counts}")

# Variant: the adopted reading (z-scored features, current defaults) without H08, H10 and H24,
# whose head-to-port distance under the fitted clock is least below that over all frames.
weak = ["H08", "H10", "H24"]
print("\nhead-to-port distance (px) under the map / over all frames:", {s: (float(pl.set_index("subject").dist_fit[s]), float(pl.set_index("subject").dist_all_frames[s])) for s in weak})
for k, V in FEAT.items():
    Vk = V[~np.isin(BW[k], weak)]
    Vk = Vk.loc[:, Vk.std() > 0]
    counts, _ = tsne_counts(PCA(30, random_state=0).fit_transform(((Vk - Vk.mean()) / Vk.std()).values))
    print(f"{k} without {weak}: {len(Vk)} trials, clusters by seed {counts}, at target {sum(c == target[k] for c in counts)} of 5")
print(f"\nnotebook ran in {(time.time() - started) / 60:.1f} min")

Result: partially reproduced. On 1319 sucrose and 688 shock trials from the 21 sessions with an aligned pose clock, no reading gives both counts: each of the four readings meets one count and not the other. With z-scored features, sucrose trials give 7 clusters for 5 of 5 seeds under the installed defaults (7, 7, 8, 7, 8 under the 2020 defaults, 3 of 5), and shock trials give 3 for 5 of 5 (4, 3, 4, 3, 3 under the 2020 defaults), never 5. With raw features, sucrose trials give 6 for 5 of 5 (7, 5, 7, 5, 6 under the 2020 defaults) and shock trials 5 for 5 of 5 (5, 5, 5, 6, 7 under the 2020 defaults, 3 of 5). The raw-feature counts are not stable: on the raw features the 3 largest features carry 95% (sucrose) and 98% (shock) of the variance and the 10 largest all of it, and with the installed defaults an exact PCA gives 8 and 5 clusters, and multiplying each feature by 1 + 1e-9 noise gives 7 and 7. With z-scored features the same changes give 7 and 4 clusters: the sucrose count stays at 7 and the shock count moves from 3 to 4, below 5 either way. The reading adopted is z-scored features with the installed defaults (7 and 3): the sucrose count holds and the shock count does not, as with the 2020 defaults; with raw features it is the reverse. Without H08, H10 and H24, whose pose clock is checked least well (head-to-port distance 29.0, 27.7 and 38.4 px under the map against 35.1, 34.8 and 46.8 px over all frames), the adopted reading gives 5 and 4. The trials rest on a pose clock fitted to the data, and the count of the sucrose trials also moves with the sessions included.

Summary¶

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

Claim Outcome
fig3k-nt-sensor-sucrose-increase not reproduced (higher late in every reading, but p = 0.093 with the first 16 trials; p = 0.0046 with all trials only under the per-trial z-score and trial-averaged fit)
fig3l-nt-sensor-airpuff-decrease not reproduced (right direction, p = 0.074 at best)
fig3-nt-sensor-early-dip not reproduced (sucrose below zero, airpuff above)
fig4-recording-count partially reproduced (31 mice against 30; 1902 or 1739 units against 685)
fig4c-photoidentification blocked, metadata_insufficient (the "fake" block evokes responses in most units, and no block or projection labels)
fig4d-seven-clusters blocked, methods_underspecified (7 clusters only with an 820 ms smoothing window)
fig5dh-behavior-clusters partially reproduced (7 sucrose clusters, 3 shock clusters, adopted reading; no reading gives both)
13 claims needing group or projection labels blocked, metadata_insufficient
19 claims on experiments not in the dandiset blocked, data_missing

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The photometry cues are taken as CS-US trials with the US 2 s after onset, since the files mark neither the US nor unpaired cues; the photometry z-score is run with per-trial and session baselines; the clustering smoothing window is run over a range since MATLAB's smoothing factor cannot be reproduced; the units are the files' units, not sorted single units; the fake phototagging block is taken as the first one, as the Methods order them; the pose is put on the trial clock by a linear map fitted to the port entries, in 21 of 29 sessions; tsfresh is the current version, not 0.16.0, even under the 2020 t-SNE defaults, and the t-SNE defaults and feature scaling are run both ways.

What was found about the dataset. The files carry no CRISPR or control label and no tagged projection, which most of the paper's electrophysiology findings need; the units are not sorted single units (frequent sub-millisecond intervals, spikes shared between units, 64 units in most sessions); H17's spike times stop at 249 s of a 12118 s recording; the pose has no timestamps and on its nominal clock of 15 frames per second the head reaches the port up to 192 s (median 80 s) away from the port entries, a drift that a rate factor of about 0.988 removes in 21 sessions; there are 31 mice where the paper has 30, and two of them may not be recorded on their last day; six sessions have no neutral CS though the description says 2:1:1; the two light blocks are not labelled fake and real, and both evoke short-latency responses in most units (1353 and 1243 of 1902); 27 files hold confocal images of the PVT with no channel or group label; the photometry series interleaves three frame types at 60 Hz in one series, in one session the LED labels move by one frame against the data, the cue events last 2 s where the Methods give 4 s, and no event marks the US or unpaired cues. Only the NT sensor experiment of the photometry is deposited; the behavioral cohorts, the axon-terminal and somatic photometry, the anatomy and the slice physiology are not.
